experiment: NIST StRD Longley linear least squares (7 parameters, 16 observations, higher difficulty)

inputs.note: Data lines 61-76 are the regression input; certified values repeat in lines 31-51. CRLF bytes kept as served.
Certified values page, source of certified.json. It embeds a per-request Cloudflare token, so a fresh fetch differs in bytes; compare the values, not the hash.
Dataset landing page (reference and links); same per-request token caveat.

environment.recorded_per_run: results/run.json (Python, numpy, BLAS/LAPACK build, platform, input and output sha256, cond2(X))

outputs: draft/section.tex (cites draft/references.bib; every decimal gated against results/results.csv)
threshold_rationale: Declared before any comparison was run: a backward-stable float64 least-squares solve is guaranteed only about -log10(cond2(X) * eps) = 5.97 digits for this design matrix (cond2(X) = 4.859e9), floored to 5. Kept after the normal-equations control unexpectedly passed: no verified literature threshold above 5 was found, and a value chosen between the observed minima (7.41 and 10.93) would tune the verdict.
control_note: The naive normal equations were expected to fail (cond2(X'X) = 2.384e19 > 1/eps) but reached min LRE 7.41 in the reference run. The column-scaled cond2(X) = 4.328e4 predicts about 6.4 digits for them and 11.0 for the SVD solve (observed 10.93): the unscaled worst-case bound was pessimistic. Their per-value LREs stay in results/check-normal-equations.json.
